transcript_only_text:
Researchers  tried  to  train  dogs  faster, 
 and  what  they  found  was  the  more  delay 
 they  had  in  their  feedback  to  the  dog, 
 the  more  times  they  had  to  try  repeating 
 the  trick.  So,  that  means  that  if  you 
 say  sit  and  the  dog  sits  and  you 
 immediately  give  it  the  treat,  you  had 
 to  have  fewer  times  to  train  the  dog. 
 Whereas,  if  you  said  sit  and  then  waited 
 30  seconds,  you  had  to  have  a  lot  of 
 times  of  doing  that  before  the  dog  got 
 it.  When  we  try  to  learn  or  we're  trying 
 to  teach  somebody  else,  an  employee,  a 
 teammate,  a  child,  whatever,  we  want  the 
 delay  on  the  feedback  to  be  as  little  as 
 possible.
